title: Add an exact κ-ceiling check for the exponent assembly (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds an exact κ-ceiling check (`scripts/assembly_ceiling.py`), tests, and a short note for both the original-prefix assembly (`structured_bulk_assembly.py`) and the balanced-prefix one (`research/copied-fixed/balanced_assembly.py`). **No new κ, no existing file changed.** Both assemblies already compute this ceiling (`minimum_margin`); what is new is the closed form, a table of which constraints can fail, and the tests.

**Result.** With q = a(1−2η) (η is the backoff, `h` for balanced), the ceiling is q(1−η)/(1+q(2+η)) for the original prefix and q(1−h)/(1+q) for the balanced one. The assembly accepts κ exactly when κ is below the ceiling and nine simple conditions hold: a, β and η in range (five checks), b < 1/32, (1−β)b > a, and the two network constants positive (balanced also needs κ > 0). So the 47 constraints reduce to 11 conditions (10 for the original prefix); three carry the content: b < 1/32, (1−β)b > a, κ < ceiling.

**Why it is the same answer as the 47 constraints.**

- *A failed condition makes the reference reject:* eight of the 11 are constraints in the reference word for word; the other three equal one up to a positive factor.
- *All 11 holding makes it accept:* they imply 0 < a < (1−β)b < b < 1/32, 0 < q < a, 0 < ε < 1 and 0 < G < q (G is the ceiling). Each of the other 36 constraints is then positive because it is a positive multiple of a positive slack (e.g. `q_below_internal` = 2aη), a sum of positive terms (e.g. b−a = ((1−β)b−a) + βb; every margin is G plus a positive term), or a simple bound from a < 1/32 and η < 1/2 (e.g. 2−3η−q(1+2η) > 7/16). κ appears only in the seven margins, each G plus a positive term, so the accepted κ are exactly those below G.

The argument is elementary but **not machine-checked**; `COVERAGE` in the module has the row for every constraint.

## Validation

- 22 tests (about 3 s) check the above at finitely many exact points: agreement with both assemblies at 30 certified points and 2,400 grid points per prefix, each condition violated once, and the identities.
- `make verify-tests` and `make paired-cube-verify` pass on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 on a clean clone (the last amend changed only the note); `structured_bulk_assembly.py` is unchanged. Python 3.11 was only syntax-checked.
- **AI assistance:** written with Claude Code (Claude Sonnet 5.5 coordinating). Other Claude models (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, Fable) re-derived the implications in sympy and searched millions of exact points for counterexamples, finding none; those scripts are not committed and nothing relies on them. No human has independently verified the mathematics.
- **Credit and overlap:** RaD project (hipotures, #20), James Chang (jamesyc, #34), Zhihao Chen (#23, #29), icekylinx. PRs #168, #169, #171, #173 and #174 add a `paired_cube_assembly.py` with the same balanced arithmetic; this PR does not import it. `NOTICE`, `CONTRIBUTORS` and a Make target are left out because `Makefile`, `README.md` and `NOTICE` are hash-pinned (editing them needs a re-pin); happy to add them.
